sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Energy Flow**: Follows the **10% Law (Lindeman's Law)**, where only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level, the rest is lost as heat.
• **Trophic Levels**: The hierarchical levels in an ecosystem, comprising producers (autotrophs), consumers (heterotrophs), and decomposers (saprotrophs).
• **Unidirectionality**: Energy flow is strictly unidirectional, unlike nutrient cycling which is cyclic.
• **Key Metric**: **Biomass** and **Energy Pyramid** structures determine the stability and efficiency of the food chain.

items.definition: The increase in concentration of non-biodegradable substances (e.g., DDT, Mercury) at successive trophic levels.
The accumulation of substances in an individual organism over time, usually through absorption from the environment.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Ecosystem Services**: Food chains underpin provisioning, regulating, and supporting services.
• **Conservation Biology**: Understanding food chains is vital for 'Keystone Species' protection (e.g., Tiger conservation).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Habitat fragmentation, pollution, and climate change disrupting trophic synchrony.
• **Solutions**: Ecosystem-based management and restoration of degraded habitats.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-P-C' (Grazing: Plants-Consumers) vs 'D-D-P' (Detritus: Dead-Detritivores-Predators).
• **Decoded Meaning**: GFC starts with living plants; DFC starts with dead matter.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Bioaccumulation' (individual level) with 'Biomagnification' (trophic level). Always check the scope of the question.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Trophic Cascade' to explain how the removal of a top predator leads to ecosystem collapse.

keyTakeaways: Energy flow is unidirectional and follows the 10% law.
Detritus food chains are the primary pathway for nutrient cycling in most ecosystems.
Biomagnification is a critical indicator of environmental toxicity and ecosystem health.
